005package org.wpilib.hardware.rotation;
006
007import static org.wpilib.util.ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam;
008
009import org.wpilib.hardware.discrete.CounterBase;
010import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.EncoderJNI;
011import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.SimDevice;
012import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryLoggable;
013import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryTable;
014import org.wpilib.util.UsageReporting;
015
016/**
017 * Class to read quadrature encoders.
018 *
019 * <p>Quadrature encoders are devices that count shaft rotation and can sense direction. The output
020 * of the Encoder class is an integer that can count either up or down, and can go negative for
021 * reverse direction counting. When creating Encoders, a direction can be supplied that inverts the
022 * sense of the output to make code more readable if the encoder is mounted such that forward
023 * movement generates negative values. Quadrature encoders have two digital outputs, an A Channel
024 * and a B Channel, that are out of phase with each other for direction sensing.
025 *
026 * <p>All encoders will immediately start counting - reset() them if you need them to be zeroed
027 * before use.
028 */
029public class Encoder implements CounterBase, TelemetryLoggable, AutoCloseable {
030  private final EncodingType m_encodingType;
031
032  int m_encoder; // the HAL encoder object
033
034  /**
035   * Common initialization code for Encoders. This code allocates resources for Encoders and is
036   * common to all constructors.
037   *
038   * <p>The encoder will start counting immediately.
039   *
040   * @param aChannel The a channel.
041   * @param bChannel The b channel.
042   * @param reverseDirection If true, counts down instead of up (this is all relative)
043   */
044  private void initEncoder(
045      int aChannel, int bChannel, boolean reverseDirection, final EncodingType type) {
046    m_encoder = EncoderJNI.initializeEncoder(aChannel, bChannel, reverseDirection, type.value);
047
048    String typeStr =
049        switch (type) {
050          case X1 -> "Encoder:1x";
051          case X2 -> "Encoder:2x";
052          case X4 -> "Encoder:4x";
053          default -> "Encoder";
054        };
055    UsageReporting.reportUsage("IO[" + aChannel + "," + bChannel + "]", typeStr);
056  }
057
058  /**
059   * Encoder constructor. Construct a Encoder given a and b channels.
060   *
061   * <p>The encoder will start counting immediately.
062   *
063   * @param channelA The 'a' SmartIO channel.
064   * @param channelB The 'b' SmartIO channel.
065   * @param reverseDirection represents the orientation of the encoder and inverts the output values
066   *     if necessary so forward represents positive values.
067   */
068  public Encoder(final int channelA, final int channelB, boolean reverseDirection) {
069    this(channelA, channelB, reverseDirection, EncodingType.X4);
070  }
071
072  /**
073   * Encoder constructor. Construct an Encoder given a and b channels.
074   *
075   * <p>The encoder will start counting immediately.
076   *
077   * @param channelA The 'a' SmartIO channel.
078   * @param channelB The 'b' SmartIO channel.
079   */
080  public Encoder(final int channelA, final int channelB) {
081    this(channelA, channelB, false);
082  }
083
084  /**
085   * Encoder constructor. Construct an Encoder given a and b channels.
086   *
087   * <p>The encoder will start counting immediately.
088   *
089   * @param channelA The 'a' SmartIO channel.
090   * @param channelB The 'b' SmartIO channel.
091   * @param reverseDirection represents the orientation of the encoder and inverts the output values
092   *     if necessary so forward represents positive values.
093   * @param encodingType either X1, X2, or X4 to indicate 1X, 2X or 4X decoding. If 4X is selected,
094   *     then an encoder FPGA object is used and the returned counts will be 4x the encoder spec'd
095   *     value since all rising and falling edges are counted. If 1X or 2X are selected, then a
096   *     counter object will be used and the returned value will either exactly match the spec'd
097   *     count or be double (2x) the spec'd count.
098   */
099  public Encoder(
100      final int channelA,
101      final int channelB,
102      boolean reverseDirection,
103      final EncodingType encodingType) {
104    requireNonNullParam(encodingType, "encodingType", "Encoder");
105
106    m_encodingType = encodingType;
107    initEncoder(channelA, channelB, reverseDirection, encodingType);
108  }
109
110  /**
111   * Get the FPGA index of the encoder.
112   *
113   * @return The Encoder's FPGA index.
114   */
115  public int getFPGAIndex() {
116    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderFPGAIndex(m_encoder);
117  }
118
119  /**
120   * Used to divide raw encoder counts down to the values returned by get().
121   *
122   * @return the scale factor used to convert raw encoder counts to scaled count values
123   */
124  public int getEncodingScale() {
125    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderEncodingScale(m_encoder);
126  }
127
128  @Override
129  public void close() {
130    // if (m_aSource != null && m_allocatedA) {
131    //   m_aSource.close();
132    //   m_allocatedA = false;
133    // }
134    // if (m_bSource != null && m_allocatedB) {
135    //   m_bSource.close();
136    //   m_allocatedB = false;
137    // }
138    // if (m_indexSource != null && m_allocatedI) {
139    //   m_indexSource.close();
140    //   m_allocatedI = false;
141    // }
142
143    // m_aSource = null;
144    // m_bSource = null;
145    // m_indexSource = null;
146    EncoderJNI.freeEncoder(m_encoder);
147    m_encoder = 0;
148  }
149
150  /**
151   * Gets the raw value from the encoder. The raw value is the actual count unscaled by the 1x, 2x,
152   * or 4x scale factor.
153   *
154   * @return Current raw count from the encoder
155   */
156  public int getRaw() {
157    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderRaw(m_encoder);
158  }
159
160  /**
161   * Gets the current count. Returns the current count on the Encoder. This method compensates for
162   * the decoding type.
163   *
164   * @return Current count from the Encoder adjusted for the 1x, 2x, or 4x scale factor.
165   */
166  @Override
167  public int get() {
168    return EncoderJNI.getEncoder(m_encoder);
169  }
170
171  /** Reset the Encoder distance to zero. Resets the current count to zero on the encoder. */
172  @Override
173  public void reset() {
174    EncoderJNI.resetEncoder(m_encoder);
175  }
176
177  /**
178   * Determine if the encoder is stopped. The encoder is stopped when its current rate is zero.
179   *
180   * @return True if the encoder is considered stopped.
181   */
182  @Override
183  public boolean getStopped() {
184    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderStopped(m_encoder);
185  }
186
187  /**
188   * The last direction the encoder value changed.
189   *
190   * @return The last direction the encoder value changed.
191   */
192  @Override
193  public boolean getDirection() {
194    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderDirection(m_encoder);
195  }
196
197  /**
198   * Get the distance the robot has driven since the last reset as scaled by the value from {@link
199   * #setDistancePerPulse(double)}.
200   *
201   * @return The distance driven since the last reset
202   */
203  public double getDistance() {
204    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderDistance(m_encoder);
205  }
206
207  /**
208   * Get the current rate of the encoder. Units are distance per second as scaled by the value from
209   * setDistancePerPulse().
210   *
211   * @return The current rate of the encoder.
212   */
213  public double getRate() {
214    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderRate(m_encoder);
215  }
216
217  /**
218   * Sets the time window used to calculate the encoder rate.
219   *
220   * @param windowMilliseconds The rate calculation window in milliseconds. Valid values are 5
221   *     through 255. The default is 50.
222   */
223  public void setRateWindow(int windowMilliseconds) {
224    EncoderJNI.setEncoderRateWindow(m_encoder, windowMilliseconds);
225  }
226
227  /**
228   * Set the distance per pulse for this encoder. This sets the multiplier used to determine the
229   * distance driven based on the count value from the encoder. Do not include the decoding type in
230   * this scale. The library already compensates for the decoding type. Set this value based on the
231   * encoder's rated Pulses per Revolution and factor in gearing reductions following the encoder
232   * shaft. This distance can be in any units you like, linear or angular.
233   *
234   * @param distancePerPulse The scale factor that will be used to convert pulses to useful units.
235   */
236  public void setDistancePerPulse(double distancePerPulse) {
237    EncoderJNI.setEncoderDistancePerPulse(m_encoder, distancePerPulse);
238  }
239
240  /**
241   * Get the distance per pulse for this encoder.
242   *
243   * @return The scale factor that will be used to convert pulses to useful units.
244   */
245  public double getDistancePerPulse() {
246    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderDistancePerPulse(m_encoder);
247  }
248
249  /**
250   * Set the direction sensing for this encoder. This sets the direction sensing on the encoder so
251   * that it could count in the correct software direction regardless of the mounting.
252   *
253   * @param reverseDirection true if the encoder direction should be reversed
254   */
255  public void setReverseDirection(boolean reverseDirection) {
256    EncoderJNI.setEncoderReverseDirection(m_encoder, reverseDirection);
257  }
258
259  /**
260   * Indicates this input is used by a simulated device.
261   *
262   * @param device simulated device handle
263   */
264  public void setSimDevice(SimDevice device) {
265    EncoderJNI.setEncoderSimDevice(m_encoder, device.getNativeHandle());
266  }
267
268  /**
269   * Gets the decoding scale factor for scaling raw values to full counts.
270   *
271   * @return decoding scale factor
272   */
273  public double getDecodingScaleFactor() {
274    return EncoderJNI.getEncoderDecodingScaleFactor(m_encoder);
275  }
276
277  @Override
278  public void logTo(TelemetryTable table) {
279    table.log("Velocity", getRate());
280    table.log("Distance", getDistance());
281    table.log("Distance per Tick", getDistancePerPulse());
282  }
283
284  @Override
285  public String getTelemetryType() {
286    if (m_encodingType == EncodingType.X4) {
287      return "Quadrature Encoder";
288    } else {
289      return "Encoder";
290    }
291  }
292}
